title: routing_rebuild_with_tiers guards its tiers slice only with assert — if a build ever disables asserts, a short slice becomes an OOB catalog read
evidence: assert(len(tiers) == len(t.pipe_alive), "routing_rebuild_with_tiers: tier view must be per-pipe-slot")
detail: The exported seam's only validation of `tiers` is an assert; the tier values then index the catalog unguarded (`nd := dist[cur] + cat.pipe_tiers[tiers[pi]].cost`, routing.odin:201, and `c := cat.pipe_tiers[tiers[pi]].cost`, routing.odin:240). Odin release builds can pass -disable-assert; no current script/CI does (verified), and both callers pass matching lengths (parallel arrays append in lockstep), so this is latent today. With asserts elided, a future caller passing a short tiers slice reads tiers[pi] out of bounds and indexes cat.pipe_tiers with garbage.
recommended_fix: Replace the assert with a real length check that fails the proc (return typed error or clamp) so the cross-package seam stays memory-safe under every build configuration.

title: The new preview demo verb truncates u64 pipe ids to u32 without a range check — an oversized id silently names a different pipe
detail: parse_uint returns u64; `u32(fid)` silently truncates values above 2^32-1 (e.g. 4294967297 becomes 1), so an out-of-range demo directive can collide with a live pipe id and render a preview for the wrong pipe — a golden blessed via `harness save` would pin a mislabeled card. The identical truncation exists in the pre-existing draw/spawn/demolish/emphasis/lane verbs, so the new verb extends a consistent but unchecked parse boundary.
recommended_fix: Reject ids that do not fit u32 (check fid > max(u32) alongside !okid) in the preview verb's parse, and ideally the same for the sibling verbs.
